summary: Iteration 5: End-to-end validation of Module 1 major fix batch (country-code + digits-only phones, duplicate-mobile server check, Google incomplete-profile flow, IST timestamps, series consumption discipline, forgot/reset, 4-min idle session timeout, /login vs /signup card ordering). Backend pytest suite (30/30 passing) + browser flow (layout, PhoneInput filters, full email signup -> /account, profile landline edit +44, duplicate-mobile 409 on profile). Series moved from 15 -> 21 with exactly one increment per successful create (email + Google), never on failure/duplicate/validation error.

minor.issue: For email-registration rows written via createCustomer the country-code cells (customer_contact_mbl_cntry / customer_contact_other_cntry) are stored as numbers so the leading '+' is dropped (e.g. '+91' displayed as '91', '+1' as '1'). Rows written for Google-completed users (also via createCustomer) preserve '+91'. Landline '03312345678' is also stripped to '3312345678' when written from email flow. API/Mongo values are correct, only the sheet cell format differs. Recommend the Apps Script to force text format (setNumberFormat('@')) on customer_contact_mbl_cntry / _other_cntry / _other / _mbl columns before setValues, or prefix with a leading apostrophe when writing.

action_items: Fix Apps Script createCustomer/upsertRow to preserve leading '+' and leading zeros on phone-related columns (format the destination columns as plain text before setValues).
critical_code_review_comments: auth/service.py assert_mobile_available also matches legacy rows with no country code (contact_mobile_cntry in [None,'']). This is intentional per team note but should be revisited when legacy rows are backfilled with '+91' - once done, drop the $or branch to avoid false positives across country codes.

services/customer_series.py catches all exceptions and returns 503; consider logging the underlying Apps Script error message so ops can distinguish 'series exhausted' vs 'network' vs 'concurrent write'.
SheetsWriter uses httpx follow_redirects=True per request (creates a new AsyncClient each call). Consider a module-level client with keep-alive to reduce Apps Script latency for bursty registration.

REQUIRED_PROFILE_FIELDS omits contact_other* - correct (landline optional). But is_profile_complete only checks truthiness; the update_profile flow relies on validate_landline being called only when field is present, which is fine.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (layout /login+/signup, PhoneInput filters, full signup->account, profile landline update, duplicate mobile 409)

test_credentials: test.customer@madamboutique.in / Madam@1234 (unchanged). +91 9876543210 used by seed - kept for duplicate tests.
seed_data_creation: Registered 5+ QA email users (qa.*@example.org) and 1 QA google user via API (CUST-000015..CUST-000020). Registered 1 QA UI user via browser (CUST-000021). All Mongo qa.* records deleted post-run. Per instructions, sheet rows were NOT deleted. Series ended at 21.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Series is now at 21 (next customer_no = CUST-000021... wait, CUST-000021 was UI test - so next = CUST-000022). Backend behaviour is stable. Only outstanding item is the sheet cell number-formatting for country-code / phone columns (leading '+' and '0' stripped for email-flow rows). Full 4-minute frontend inactivity redirect test was NOT executed via Playwright to save runtime, but backend idle-timeout logic is directly verified via mongosh (test_session_idle_timeout_401). If you need to validate the browser SessionGuard live, use page.wait_for_timeout(250000) after login and assert redirect to /login.
rca of the issue: Sheet number-formatting bug RCA: Google Sheets treats a purely numeric-looking string ('+91', '03312345678') as a number and drops the leading '+' / '0' unless the target cell is formatted as text. Google-flow rows for the two google users happened to be written into cells that were already text-formatted (either manual formatting on those specific ranges or the flow going through a different code path that pre-formats). Fix: In Code.gs upsertRow_ / createCustomer_, after computing target row and before setValues, call sheet.getRange(row, 1, 1, headers.length).setNumberFormat('@') OR force text by prefixing with an apostrophe for the four phone columns.
